questions.question:
For a given gas at \(1\) atm pressure, the RMS speed of the molecules is \(200~\text{m/s}\) at \(127^\circ\text{C}.\) At \(2\) atm pressure and at \(227^\circ\text{C},\) the RMS speed of the molecules will be:

1.\(100~\text{m/s}\)2.\(80\sqrt{5}~\text{m/s}\)
3.\(100\sqrt{5}~\text{m/s}\)4.\(80~\text{m/s}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: The RMS speed depends on the temperature but not on the pressure. Step 1: Find the relation between the RMS speed and the temperature. The RMS velocity of a gas molecule is given by; \({v}_{\text{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3{RT}}{{~m}}}\) \(\Rightarrow {v}_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt{{T}}\) Step 2: Find the final RMS speed of the molecules. For two different cases: \(\Rightarrow \frac{{v}_{\text{rms}{_1}}}{{v}_{\text{rms} _2}}=\sqrt{\frac{{T}_1}{{~T}_2}}\) \(\Rightarrow \frac{200}{{v}_{\text{rms} _2}}=\sqrt{\frac{400}{500}}=\sqrt{\frac{4}{5}} \) \(\Rightarrow {v}_{\text{rms}_2}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2} \times 200 \) \(\Rightarrow {v}_{\text{rms}_2}=100{\sqrt{5}}~\text{ms}^{-1} \) Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
An ideal gas is confined in a closed container and slowly heated. As the temperature rises, which of the following statements are correct?

(A)The mean free path of gas molecules decreases.
(B)The mean collision time between the molecules decreases.
(C)The mean free path remains unchanged.
(D)The mean collision time remains unchanged.
Choose the correct option from the given ones:
1.(C) and (D) only
2.(A) and (B) only
3.(A) and (D) only
4.(B) and (C) only
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\lambda=\dfrac{V}{\sqrt{2} \pi {d}^2 {N}}\) Step:Analyse each option one by one. The mean free path of molecules of an ideal gas is given by; \(\lambda=\dfrac{V}{\sqrt{2} \pi {d}^2 {N}}= \dfrac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 P}~~~~~~~~~[\because PV = nk_B T]\) where,\(V=\) Volume of container,\(N=\) No of molecules The mean collision time is given by; \(\tau = \dfrac{\lambda}{\text{average speed}}\) Since the gas is heated slowly in a closed container, the volume remains constant. So, the mean free path is unchanged. In other words, as temperature rises, the pressure inside the container will increase proportionally. From the mean free path formula, since both \(T\) and \(P\) increase proportionally, the mean free path remains unchanged. The mean free path remains the same, but the average molecular speed increases with temperature. So, the mean collision time decreases. Therefore, the correct statements are(B) and (C) only. Hence, option (4) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The mass of a hydrogen molecule is \(3.32 \times 10^{-27}~\text{kg}.\) If \(10^{23}\) hydrogen molecules strike, per second, a fixed wall of area \(2~\text{cm}^2\) at an angle of \(45^\circ\) to the normal, and rebound elastically with a speed of \(10^3~\text{m/s},\) then the pressure on the wall is nearly:
1. \( 2.35 \times 10^3 ~\text{N/m}^2 \)
2. \(4.70 \times 10^3 ~\text{N/m}^2 \)
3. \(2.35 \times 10^2 ~\text{N/m}^2 \)
4. \(4.70 \times 10^2 ~\text{N/m}^2 \)
questions.explanation:
Hint: \(P=\frac{F}{A}=\frac{n\times 2 m \times v \times \cos (\theta)}{A}\) Step: Find the pressure on the wall. When a molecule strikes the wall and reflects back elastically, the change in momentum in the \(x\text-\)direction (the direction normal to the wall) can be calculated as follows; The component of velocity in the \(x\text-\)direction before collision is given by; \(\Rightarrow v_x=v \cos (\theta)=v \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{10^3}{\sqrt{2}} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\) The change in momentum for one molecule is given by; \(\Delta p=m \times \left[v_x-\left(-v_x\right)\right]=m\times\left(2 v_x\right)=2 m v \cos (\theta)\) The total rate of change of momentum for \(n\) molecules striking the wall per second is given by; Total change in momentum \(=n \times \Delta p=n \times 2 m v \cos (\theta)=n \times 2 m \times \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} \) The force \(F\) exerted on the wall is equal to the total rate of change of momentum is given by; \(\Rightarrow F=n \times 2 m \times v \times \cos (\theta)\) The pressure \(P\) is defined as force per unit area is given by; \(\Rightarrow P=\frac{F}{A}=\frac{n\times 2 m \times v \times \cos (\theta)}{A}\) \(P=\frac{10^{23}\times 2\times\left(3.32 \times 10^{-27}\right) \times \left(10^3\right) \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{2 \times 10^{-4}} \) \(P=10^{23} \times 3.32 \times 10^{-23} \times\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{3.32}{\sqrt{2}} \times 10^3 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2 \) \(\Rightarrow P \approx 2.35 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

A gas mixture consists of \(3\) moles of oxygen and \(5\) moles of argon at temperature \(T.\) Assuming the gases to be ideal and the oxygen bond to be rigid, the total internal energy (in units of \(RT\)) of the mixture is:
1. \(11\)
2. \(15\)
3. \(20\)
4. \(13\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(U=\frac{fnRT}{2}\) Step: Find the total internal energy of the mixture​​​​​​. The number of degrees of freedom for diatomic oxygen considering the oxygen bond is rigid: \(f_1=5\) The number of degrees of freedom for monoatomic argon: \( f_2=3 \) The total internal energy of the mixture of gas is given by; \(U=\frac{1}{2} n_1 f_1 R T+\frac{1}{2} n_2 f_2 R T \) Subsitute the known values we get; \(U=\left(\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 5+\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 3\right) R T \) \(\Rightarrow U=15RT\) Hence, option (2) is the correct answer.
